_README: Rate assumptions for container_model.py. Anything marked _verify must be
confirmed by a licensed customs broker against the entry-date HTSUS before
you wire money. Tariff rates in this space changed four times in 18 months.
Customs value = transaction value (broadly the FOB price paid to the
supplier). Ocean freight is NOT in the customs value for US entries, which
is why it sits in `logistics` and is not duty-bearing.

hts_classification.basis: CBP CROSS rulings NY N303868 and NY N267728 classify roll-formed, punched steel channel/profile under 7216.91.00 (cold-formed from flat-rolled). '0010' is the drilled/notched/punched statistical suffix -- framing studs have punched service holes.
hts_classification._verify: Get a BINDING RULING from CBP before the first entry. A ruling is free and takes ~30-90 days. Guessing the code is how importers end up in a 19 USC 1592 penalty case.

section_232.basis: Proclamation 11021, 'Strengthening Actions Taken To Adjust Imports of Aluminum, Steel, and Copper', signed 2026-04-02, effective 12:01am EDT 2026-04-06. 50% top tier on articles made entirely or almost entirely of steel, assessed on FULL customs value. Federal Register 2026-06960.
section_232._verify: Proclamation 2026-11314 (June 2026) further adjusted the regime, and BIS opened another derivative-inclusions comment window 2026-08-06 (FR 2026-15961). Confirm the operative rate at entry date.

section_301.basis: China Section 301 List 3 rate. Steel articles of Ch.72 were broadly covered on List 3 at 25%.
section_301._verify: UNVERIFIED for 7216.91.0010 specifically. Confirm against the USTR list and the HTSUS Ch.99 subheading before relying on it.

ieepa.basis: The Supreme Court struck down IEEPA-based tariffs on 2026-02-20; the reciprocal and 'fentanyl' tariffs on China were terminated and CBP opened the CAPE refund portal 2026-04-20. These no longer stack.
ieepa._verify: Watch for replacement authority. The administration retains Section 122, Section 338 and expanded 301 options. This line can come back.

mfn._verify: UNVERIFIED. Column 1 General rate for 7216.91.0010 -- many Ch.72 lines are Free, but confirm on hts.usitc.gov.

ad_cvd.basis: No AD/CVD order identified that plainly names cold-formed steel framing from China as of this writing.
ad_cvd._verify: THIS IS THE BUSINESS-ENDING RISK. AD/CVD is deposited at entry and FINALLY ASSESSED at administrative review, often 2-3 years later, and the importer owes the difference retroactively with interest. Rates on Chinese steel cases have exceeded 100%. Check for new petitions and scope/anti-circumvention rulings BEFORE EVERY ORDER, not once.

mpf_hmf._verify: MPF ad valorem rate and the min/max cap adjust annually for inflation. Confirm current figures.

ben_claim.name: As described verbally (reverse-engineered)
ben_claim.notes: Ben's stated numbers: ~$11,000 all-in landed, sell at ~$22,000. This scenario back-solves what the FOB invoice would have to be for $11,000 to be true under the CURRENT duty stack. If the implied FOB is below the raw steel value of a container, the quote is not what he thinks it is.

base_case.name: Realistic container, current duty stack
base_case.notes: A 40HC of cold-formed steel framing at a plausible FOB value, run through the verified Section 232 + Section 301 stack, with real cut-shop and delivery cost added. Replace fob_invoice_value with the actual supplier quote.

adcvd_shock.name: AD/CVD order lands mid-stream
adcvd_shock.notes: Same container, but a petition succeeds and a combined AD/CVD deposit rate attaches. Models the retroactive-assessment risk: this is what a demand letter looks like two years after you already sold and spent the money.

domestic_alternative.name: Buy domestic, distribute only
domestic_alternative.notes: No import, no duty, no AD/CVD tail, no code-compliance argument, no importer product liability. Thinner margin, but the business is legal-risk-free and can bid Buy America work. This is the control case every import scenario must beat on a RISK-ADJUSTED basis, not just on margin.
